bug_semantics: rConfig deliberately disabled Laravel self-registration with Auth::routes(['register' => false]), but a later bare Auth::routes() call registered the framework's default registration endpoints again. An unauthenticated POST /register therefore reached RegisterController, whose create() method omitted role; the users.role database column defaulted to Admin, and the RegistersUsers flow authenticated the newly created account. The attacker consequently obtained a logged-in Administrator account without invitation, approval, or prior credentials.
flaw_origin: The smallest first-writer is 5ae01b3781de867baad1a8aa8aebfc3448812f68. In the multiple-SSO feature commit, routes/web.php gained the single causally decisive line Auth::routes(); between the new SAML logout and provider redirect routes. The already-present disabled-registration call, framework registration controller, and Admin column default made that new route dangerous, but they did not expose registration while the only auth route declaration had register=false. The candidate's immediate parent 6202a5d9e061fce98de25ec8b62a4973c0dffd35 has no bare call.
ai_marker: absent — the raw commit object for BIC 5ae01b3781de867baad1a8aa8aebfc3448812f68 names human author and committer danielrConfig <daniel@rconfig.com>, and its complete message has no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, AI-tool, or bot trailer. The Claude co-author trailer on the later fix d3fe04fc9d2e1f892b9e21f037e4104badd565e3 is not evidence about the BIC.
evidence: First-party advisory https://github.com/rconfig/rconfig/security/advisories/GHSA-w3hx-9cxg-5ccr describes the duplicate bare Auth::routes() mechanism, the inherited registration scaffold, the Admin role default, affected range >=8.0.0,<8.2.10, and patched version 8.2.10. The assigned global advisory https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-3xhw-7rxv-vwc7 / CVE-2026-77915 describes the same mechanism but its prose says before 8.2.13; repository history and the first-party advisory establish the actual 8.2.10 patch boundary. `git log -L 19,19:routes/web.php 5ae01b...` returns only 5ae01b3781de867baad1a8aa8aebfc3448812f68 and the hunk `@@ -11,0 +19,1 @@` / `+Auth::routes();`. `git ls-tree` plus `git cat-file -p` shows candidate blob 59bea0ad016c9dba5b26460ffeed896632f72edf contains both Auth::routes(['register' => false]) and the later Auth::routes(), while immediate-parent blob d374100b5aabd44348863b59163011513f7f8529 contains only the disabled-registration declaration; this directly verifies parent absence. Candidate RegisterController.php uses RegistersUsers and User::create with name, email, and password only, while database/migrations/2020_09_06_105623_update_role_field_default_value.php sets role default to Admin. `git cat-file -p 5ae01b...` proves the BIC is a one-parent public commit with parent 6202a5d9e061fce98de25ec8b62a4973c0dffd35 and no AI attribution; the GitHub associated-pulls endpoint returns [], so there are no reconstructable public squash members. `git diff-tree` shows the route addition is part of that direct multiple-SSO commit. Release ancestry checks show 5ae01b... is an ancestor of both core-8.0.0 (tag commit 5a3718ccb441e1330f2d9399e845e88e1bc0087d) and core-8.2.9 (6893037b3635e5385bc8de21af1e4eeac10adad9); the core-8.0.0 route blob 9e7cb388da91091dc58b42692bab275e175e03ae and core-8.2.9 blob 6f7aa5034266766f0d53507489a87f8621a6f1de both contain the bare call. Fix commit d3fe04fc9d2e1f892b9e21f037e4104badd565e3 directly removes that call, deletes RegisterController, changes the role default to User, and adds regression coverage. It is absent from core-8.2.9 and is an ancestor of core-8.2.10 (tag commit da649a1c22c2bc75adeda9e62daef24e3cd84903); the core-8.2.10 route blob 321d68cf1725ed31d3b19eb74710e655a827de75 contains only Auth::routes(['register' => false]).
reasoning: The lifecycle is closed from introduction through release and repair. Registration was intentionally disabled before the BIC. Commit 5ae01b... added a second, unqualified Laravel auth-route declaration while implementing SSO; Laravel registers rather than retracts the default endpoints, so the new declaration reopened POST /register. The existing controller then inserted a user without a role and the existing schema supplied Admin, after which RegistersUsers logged the caller in. Line history identifies 5ae01b... as the direct first-writer, and direct comparison to its immediate parent proves the vulnerable bare call was absent there. This is smaller and more causal than treating the older controller/default or any later move/refactor/release commit as the BIC. Tag ancestry and route blobs place the flaw in the first 8.x release and through core-8.2.9, while d3fe04f... removes it in core-8.2.10; this concrete boundary resolves the later global advisory's imprecise 'before 8.2.13' wording in favor of first-party and repository evidence. Finally, only the BIC commit object controls attribution: it is authored and committed by danielrConfig and has no AI marker. The AI co-author trailer on the fix cannot retroactively attribute the BIC, so the closed verdict is NOT_AI.
